questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I would like some advice about a letter from my landlord, Weidgrund Services Ltd in Kreuzlingen.

What bothers me most is the reason they give. Mr David Weber writes only that the rents for similar flats along the lake have "risen considerably" and that mine should be brought into line with them. There is nothing in the letter about their own costs having gone up, no mention of interest or running costs, and nothing about any renovation or new service. Nobody has done any work in the building for as long as I've lived here.

The letter itself is dated 1 August 2026. It says that the rent for my flat at Seestrasse 104 will go up from the current CHF 2440 a month by CHF 262.50, so I would be paying an extra CHF 3150 a year. It came on their official form with Mr Weber's signature and says the new rent is to be paid from the beginning of December.

For me this is a lot of money and I find it hard to believe I should simply accept it because other people pay more. What can I do, and is there a deadline I need to watch?

Best regards,
Peter Hürlimann
